title: Soulframe opens up for everyone next week as the Warframe devs prepare the fantasy action RPG for one of its 'biggest, most violent' updates ever next month
summary: Verse of the Veilands will radically change the structure of the game so it's easier for new players to follow.
body: After three years of invite-only playtests, Soulframe is opening its doors to everyone next week on November 6. If you've been waiting to see what the developers of Warframe are doing with a fantasy action RPG, you'll finally be able to jump in and see for yourself. The transition to an open alpha will be followed by a massive transformation to the structure of the game later in November. Midrath, Soulframe's big open landmass, won't be the verdant, almost chill, place it used to be: The entire area will be corrupted and it's your job to bring it back to life. "You're going to enter a game that is much more unforgiving and harsh at first glance," creative director Geoff Crookes explained in a recent presentation attended by PC Gamer. This update, Prelude 17 or Verse of the Veillands, is a huge shift for Soulframe, but an important one that will help new players acclimate to the world. Crookes said the goal is to improve the onboarding experience and to give players "much more ownership" over their decisions early on. It won't be fully finished yet, however, so what's in there today is just "the functional bones" of what will come in the final game. Feedback from players who strugg…

title: A Daedalic adventure classic is free on GOG
summary: A Daedalic adventure classic is free on GOG
body: We previewed A New Beginning , a Daedalic point-and-click adventure about saving the world from environmental catastrophe, all the way back in 2011, and it seemed promising: "Neither preachy nor educational," despite its ecological angle, but "pure sci-fi, involving a clash between one magic power-source that nukes the Earth, and a race to get it replaced with another magic one that turns simple algae into the ultimate fuel." A good bit of time-travel, too. That's always fun. That promise paid off in the final release—not one of Daedalic's most memorable games, but a solid point-and-clicker from a studio that was at the time beginning to establish itself as one of the masters of the genre. And all of this is relevant to you because A New Beginning: Final Cut is now free on GOG. I'm not sure why it's free, exactly: The giveaway isn't explicitly connected to GOG's currently-underway 18 th Anniversary Sale (which is worth checking out in its own right, as always there are some very cheap deals to be had), nor is A New Beginning what I'd call a Halloween-themed game—although the prospect of ecological collapse driven by climate change that humanity seems studiously determined to ignor…

title: This brutal Fallout 4 horror mod turns the Commonwealth into Silent Hill
summary: Introduce Pyramid Head and friends to the Boston suburbs in Whispering Hills.
body: Fallout 4's overworld was always missing something that the other 3D wastelands in the series offered me: a sense of bleakness and danger. There are areas of the map, like the Glowing Sea, that managed to dial up the oppression. But the unforgiving horror mod Whispering Hills makes the whole region eerie and mysterious. And I honestly love that. Presented by (Image credit: Torn Banner) This article is brought to you by No More Room in Hell 2 . My playthrough started the same way as vanilla Fallout 4, with a tableau of mid-Century suburban domestic bliss interrupted by a tense run to Vault 111. But from there, I almost started to think my hard drive was haunted. The post-nuclear world has been reimagined with constant, dense fog and occasional torrential rain that limit your view distance to only a handful of yards. It reminded me of how Morrowind used its limited view distance to make Vvardenfell feel much bigger than it was, even if at the time it was also a technical necessity. Part of the problem with the Commonwealth overworld in unmodded Fallout 4 is that it's relatively flat and mostly green, so a lot of it feels very same-y. title: Edifier G5 Max wireless gaming headset review
summary: Lightweight, long-lasting, but lacking.
body: In the world of wireless gaming headsets, there's one spec that draws me in like a moth to a flame: battery life. Particularly 100-hour+ battery life. Wireless cans have come a long way in the last decade, but plugging them in all the time is an annoyance. If I can get away with multiple days without messing around with a cable, I usually will. Which brings me to the Edifier G5 Max . Or the Edifier Hecate G5 Max, if you believe the writing on the box. It's got an astonishing "are you really sure" battery life spec of 305-hours, which meant I had to give it a look. And now I've got one in my hands, I can confirm the battery life is impressive. Only the original HyperX Cloud Alpha Wireless comes close. But the G5 Max, for its $150 / $160 price tag, isn't quite the full ticket in other departments. For one, it comes with a remarkably boxy default sound profile, so you'll want to do some EQ tweaking in the software to sweeten it up. That's usually no big deal—except the EQ presets are as blunt as a hammer, so you'll need to play around with the sliders yourself if you want to get the most out of it. The 53 mm composite drivers are actually fairly decent once they've been fiddled with,…

title: EA reportedly canned BioWare and Mass Effect 5 to make a new Star Wars: Battlefront instead
summary: One last bitter drop in a chalice of sorrow.
body: According to Bloomberg's sources, EA saw a new Battlefront game as a less risky investment than Mass Effect Universe. This final factor joined a host of well-discussed reasons for BioWare's unfortunate demise: Andromeda's critical reception, Anthem's live service failure, Veilguard's sales struggle ( pretty good game though ), friction between the studio and EA since the very beginning, and, of course, EA's recent Saudi-Kushner-Private Equity acquisition. One other added wrinkle: BioWare apparently lost its main ally at the top of the EA org chart. Entertainment and Central Development exec Laura Miele, who historically advocated for BioWare, was "sidelined" according to Bloomberg. EA sports execs David Tinson and Cam Weber were promoted instead. The age of nerds has ended, now begins the long night of the jock. Overall, this new information doesn't radically reframe BioWare's overall story at EA, one of slow decline and mismanagement, or how most observers will interpret it through a culture war lens⁠. Was BioWare too woke? Not woke enough? For the love of god keep it out of our comments section. But now we know why the knife was finally driven home, for what it's worth. And I gu…

title: OCE players are stuck in perpetual night on WoW: Forever, but its devs are considering a fix
summary: "It's something we talked about."
body: World of Warcraft: Forever is "realmless", which has a couple of advantages for oceanic (OCE) players—who so often get the short end of the stick when it comes to MMORPGs. Blizzard has servers in Australia, so OCE players can enjoy not having terrible ping, but due to the smaller playerbase they share a lot of overlap with the North American server architecture. Which produces a unique problem: As it stands, OCE players are stuck in perpetual night. See, Forever has a 24 hour day/night cycle, so if you play during the evening and your timezone's matched to the server, the sun will set in Azeroth roughly at the time it would outside your window. But since OCE players are very much not local to North America… the curse of endless night persists. As explained here on the WoW forums: "Because our servers share North American clock cycles, playing after work means the game is locked in pitch black. Log on at 7 pm? Midnight. Saturday afternoon? Dark. Unless you ruin your sleep schedule to play at 4 am, you practically never see the sun in Kalimdor." title: Patrick Stewart, Star Trek and Shakespeare legend, has died
summary: Stewart died at age 86 after "a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer's Disease."
body: Patrick Stewart, the classically-trained actor who gained worldwide fame in the 1980s as Captain Jean-Luc Picard on Star Trek: The Next Generation and later as Professor Charles Xavier in the X-Men film series, has died. A message posted on Stewart's official X account said his passing came "following a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer's Disease and Lewy Body Dementia." Stewart joined the Royal Shakespeare Company in 1966, and took his first television role a year later on the long-running British series Coronation Street. He debuted on Broadway in 1971, and subsequently appeared in several feature films. body: After 23 mainline games, there are far more Call of Duty maps than anyone can reasonably remember. That's why I'm impressed it took just one screenshot for several fans (with back pain, presumably) to clock that an upcoming Modern Warfare 4 map is actually a remake of a map that's over 20 years old. Backstab, the new 6v6 map arriving on November 6, is a dead ringer for Burgundy , first seen in Call of Duty 2 way back in 2005. That means Backstab is older than the teenagers currently playing Call of Duty—do with that information what you will. A number of people noticed this around the same time, but I'll credit Reddit user wizward64 for providing helpful visuals. (Image credit: Activision Blizzard) Apologies to the reader typing "This was a classic, show some respect!", but there's no way I would've noticed the resemblance on my own. body: PUBG, the battle royale that lets you wear a frying pan on your ass to keep it from getting shot off, is being made into a live action series for Netflix. Narrative isn't really PUBG's strong point, but this one might be interesting for one big reason: Donald Glover is set to write, direct, and executive produce the series, and will also star in it. Stephen Glover, Donald's brother and frequent collaborator, is also attached to the project as writer and executive producer. Glover has won numerous awards over the years for writing, acting, and music (under his stage name Childish Gambino), to the point that "list of awards and nominations received by Donald Glover" has its own remarkably lengthy Wikipedia page . Highlights include two Primetime Emmy awards, two Golden Globes, five Grammy Awards, two Peabody Awards, and five Writers Guild of America Awards. The upside of PUBG not having a strong pre-existing story like, say, Halo or Fallout is that it affords creators the opportunity to do their own thing, and as I said, that could be very interesting indeed with Glover at the helm. title: 'AAA publishers are abusing early access,' Denis Dyack says, and that's making things harder for everyone else
summary: Dyack believes that games like Subnautica 2 are "skewing player expectations" for early access games.
body: Denis Dyack, known for his work on games including Blood Omen: Legacy of Kain and Eternal Darkness: Sanity's Requiem, says big game developers are "abusing early access" by using it as a marketing tool for highly polished games that are ready for full release anyway. That, Dyack believes, has shifted expectations for early access releases overall, and made life more difficult for indie developers who rely on the process to actually get their games finished and launched. "They can put up a polished product and rake in cash," Dyack told GamesIndustry . "It's a marketing beat for them. So, that leaves players often expecting a near-perfect game that, in our opinion, defeats the purpose of early access, which is a collaborative development process based on player feedback. "AAA publishers are abusing early access, skewing player expectations in such a way that it heavily disadvantages smaller independent developers." Dyack said games like Subnautica 2 and Path of Exile are "drastically changing the landscape and players' expectations," which in turn has led to "significant barriers to entry" for less polished games like Dyack's current project, Deadhaus Sonata , which is now in early …

title: YouTuber buys and turns 32 GB of laptop DDR5 into desktop RAM for just $175
summary: They then overclocked it.
body: In this week's 'what the memory crisis is doing to people' news, a YouTuber has recently bought 32 GB of DDR5 laptop memory online and successfully converted it into memory for their desktop. Overall, it cost them just $175 ($120 for the memory and $55 for extra components). That's a bit of a bargain, as 32 GB DDR5 dual-channel memory is fetching upwards of $500 on Newegg right now. Blighted Agent took to their YouTube channel to share the process, where they purchased two SO-DIMM sticks of 16 GB DDR5 memory on Facebook Marketplace (presumably salvaged from a dead laptop). From here, they put a stick on a preheater, then removed the BIOS chip, the SPD chip and all eight of its memory chips. Buying new DDR5 DIMM PCBs and heatsinks off AliExpress, they cleaned the factory unleaded solder on the laptop memory, then soldered them onto the new PCBs. It's an impressive feat that requires reballing the memory chips with a stencil, a very precise procedure. Blighted Agent says, "You want a thin layer of flux, not too much or not too little. If you do too little, the balls might not reflow properly. If you do too much, they might bridge and cause problems". Effectively, those solder balls …

title: I'm calling it: GTA 6 is officially an immersive sim, based on what you can do with NPCs
summary: If I see a video of Lucia stacking crates to get over a wall I'm gonna lose it.
body: I don't mean to be contrarian (which is rare for me), but I've been generally unfazed by the hype for Grand Theft Auto 6. It's not that I don't think it'll be good—I'm actually damn near certain it will—it's just that none of what Rockstar has focused on so far in its marketing speaks to me all that much. Anyway, throw those equanimous sentiments out the window, because an anecdote from Edge magazine's new mondo-feature on GTA 6 has convinced me this game is actually an immersive sim, and now I'm bouncing off the walls in anticipation. Chatting about his experience actually playing the game, Rockstar head of development Phil Hooker told a story about the time he deployed a bit of unorthodox crowd control to prepare a store for a heist. "Recently I was robbing a store that was full of people," said Hooker. "I wanted to get rid of them, because they'd be witnesses who would cause me trouble." What did he do? Well, in GTAs of yore, your options would have been pretty limited, but GTA 6's dovetailing systems gave our man an opportunity. title: Where to find the Hokubo region Treasure Hunt in Forza Horizon 6
summary: Track this chest to some greenhouses.
body: (Image credit: Playground Games) Key deets (Image credit: Playground Games) 🚘 The treasure chest is in central Hokubo at a greenhouse in the Shikisai-no-oka. Spring has arrived in Forza Horizon 6 's Horizon Meets series, which means a new Treasure Hunt chest to find for some seasonal points, which will help you earn some progress towards the new cars on offer. This week's treasure chest is in central Hokubo by a greenhouse at the Shikisai-no-oka—the distinctive field of colourful strips you can see on the map. To find it: Drive along the road going northwest through Shikisai-no-oka's fields. When the road turns east, look for the greenhouses on your left. The chest is between these, as shown on the map above. Head there and smash the chest to get 100,000 credits, 5,000 XP, and three Season Progress. title: Havn HS 360 review
summary: Stunning simplicity.
body: The Havn HS 360 is a familiar sight. More or less the same design as the company's first case, the HS 420, it's just a touch smaller. That's no bad thing; the HS 420 earned a 90% score from me due to its ability to hide most of the ugliness that comes with the usual pile of cables and connectors behind its retro futurist style facade. I feel just as positively about this slightly shrunken version too. The HS 360 is available in two versions, with or without vertical GPU mounting; and two colours, black or white. I've here two cases for review, covering all the options, and I've decided to put them to the test with rival builds. Namely to get a feel for the process of building with the different GPU mounting solutions, but also satiate my longstanding desire to build yin and yang gaming PCs. Dark and light. AMD and Nvidia. title: If Kane Parsons does make a Backrooms sequel then it'll be to 'poke at' aspects of the first film that 'didn't feel like it accurately spoke to the cultural core of Backrooms'
summary: Give me The Bacteria or give me death!
body: The Backrooms left me with more questions than answers, which to be fair is exactly what I wanted from it . But, while I enjoy sustaining the mystique of this odd liminal space, I would like to see a bit more of what Parsons has to offer of his take on the backrooms—so yes, I would like a sequel. It's still touch and go whether Parsons will even revisit The Backrooms on the silver screen, but if he did there are a couple of things he'd apparently do differently: "I consider it, me advancing and doubling down on the strengths that I think are more universally recognised about the core idea," Parsons says in an interview with The Kyle Buchanan Show . "Rather than doubling down on the things or points where it didn't feel like it accurately spoke to the cultural core of Backrooms in the first film—[there are] a few little places here and there, that I would personally go out of my way to poke at a little bit." title: Phantom Blade Zero dev says don't get the latest Nvidia drivers
summary: Luckily, rolling back drivers is pretty easy.
body: Phantom Blade Zero , the highly anticipated wuxia action RPG, is finally out in the world, and if you're planning on playing it on an Nvidia graphics card, maybe consider skipping the latest Nvidia driver update. Yes, that's the opposite of developer S-Game's pre-launch advice . Today, the Phantom Blade Zero devs took to the Steam page with a post titled "Reason and Madness" recounting the history of the dev team, previous works, and how Phantom Blade Zero came to be. This is followed up with three announcements: a recommendation to download the 5 GB day one patch, encouragement to try the game on handhelds and lower-end/mid-range PCs, and, finally, advice not to use the latest Nvidia driver, 621.01. It says, "Based on our testing, version 617.42 currently offers the best experience in Phantom Blade Zero. If you’ve installed a driver newer than 617.42, we recommend rolling back to 617.42 and choosing the clean installation option. Please stay on this version until Nvidia releases its next driver update, which we expect to arrive soon." title: For the second time this year, Galax says it's not closing down: Palit-owned graphics card brand 'continues to operate as usual'
summary: Reports of the brand's death have been greatly exaggerated.
body: Galax has come out in defence of its continued existence for the second time this year, following a report that incorrectly claimed the graphics card brand was closing down its factory. In a report by El Chapuzas Informatico, citing industry sources, Palit was claimed to be closing the Galax factory. This is said to be occurring at the same time as a major reorganisation of the Galax and KFA2 brands. Galax, a subsidiary brand of Palit, has expressly denied this claim. In, the company says its business operations are "continuing as normal". "Galax continues to operate as usual," a statement under both Palit and Galax letterheads, published on the Galax website , says. "No manufacturing facilities have been shut down, and Galax products remain available through our sales channels in both domestic and international markets. That bit about internal reorganising of the Galax and KFA2 brands has some truth to it. We know that from Palit's previous statement on a rumoured Galax closure. Yep, Galax has been rumoured for chop before, and not too long ago. It last happened in April, 2026 . Back then, it was speculated that Galax was shuttering and Palit was taking over. title: All Honor Among Thieves answers in Phantom Blade Zero
summary: Describe the brother's letter to The Gentle Thief.
body: The Honor Among Thieves quest in Phantom Blade Zero is relatively short—you kill an enemy in the Crimson Forest who drops a letter, which you then deliver to his brother in the Thieves Camp a little further down the trail after Jing Ye. The brother, however, can't read, and demands you answer some questions about its contents to prove it's genuine. The answers to his questions are: Stole a landowner's belt. Butterfly. The letter never said. His fate is unknown. Don't worry if you get an answer wrong, he'll just end the conversation and you'll have to talk to him again. These answers are, of course, in the letter itself. Look for the Wulin Tales section of the archive and then the 8th entry, Blood Letter from the Nimble Thief. Answer all three correctly and you'll get the Silent Wrap accessory, which reduces noise from assassinations and movement by 40%, though you can upgrade this further once you unlock polishing in the Village of Lu. title: How to beat the Aberrant Three-Faced Puppet in Phantom Blade Zero
summary: Defeat this tricky boss and complete the second part of the Triple-Threat quest.
body: The Aberrant Three-Faced Puppet is the first optional boss you can encounter in Phantom Blade Zero , but it's definitely not one you're supposed to beat when you first find it. It's definitely possible, but with no Phantom Edges and only your un-upgraded starting weapon, you don't deal anywhere near enough damage to be likely to defeat her, and won't for a while. Here are some tips that'll help you best her when you're ready: Return later : There's no rush to defeat this boss or complete the Triple Threat quest. Defeating her doesn't give you a weapon or anything that's useful in the early game, either, so there's really no reason to bang your head against the fight. To beat her when you first meet her, you basically have to no-hit the entire thing, so it's not really worth it. As you can see in the video above, I returned later in the game and the fight was much more manageable. Upgrade your weapon and polish your accessories : In particular, I recommend the Ancient Armor Fragment, Jewel's Knot, and Resonance Talisman for increased damage negation, HP, and Sha-Chi.
